biography: Rory McKean's journey began not on a racetrack, but on the windswept Isle of Man. Growing up surrounded by the legendary TT course ignited a passion for speed and precision. Instead of bikes, however, Rory found his calling in four wheels, tearing up local karting tracks with a ferocious determination that often bordered on reckless. His raw talent quickly caught the eye of Ginetta scouts, who signed him to their junior program at 19. His debut season was a rollercoaster, showcasing both dazzling overtakes and costly crashes, a pattern that would define much of his early career. Now, at 37, McKean has tempered his aggression, evolving into a seasoned competitor capable of consistent podium finishes. While a championship title has eluded him, he remains a force to be reckoned with, a true 'old school' racer in an increasingly technical sport.
drivingStyle: McKean's driving style is a blend of controlled aggression and calculated risk. He is known for his late-braking maneuvers and daring overtakes, often pushing the limits of his car and the patience of his rivals. While he has learned to manage his tires more effectively over the years, his natural instinct is to attack from the first lap, setting a relentless pace that puts immense pressure on his competitors. He excels in wet conditions, where his car control and fearlessness truly shine.

rivalries.reason: A bitter feud ignited after a controversial collision in the final corner of the 2021 Brands Hatch race, costing McKean a potential victory.
A strategic rivalry. Tanaka, known for his meticulous data analysis, represents everything McKean dislikes about modern racing, leading to frequent clashes on and off the track.
Eriksson, a calm and collected driver, has repeatedly outsmarted McKean on track with superior race management, frustrating the British driver's aggressive style.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of driving gloves, patched and repaired countless times.
Listens to a specific heavy metal track ('Ace of Spades' by Motorhead) before every race.
Refuses to talk to anyone for 30 minutes before the race, preferring to visualize the entire race in his head.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the envelope until it screams.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Spa 24 Hours with a last-lap overtake, showcasing his exceptional wet-weather driving skills and unwavering determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2016 British GT Championship finale at Donington Park due to overzealous driving, costing him the championship.
